question: Should OpenClaw publish a public OpenAPI/Swagger contract for Gateway programmatic access, and should that contract be a static artifact, a served runtime endpoint, or a documented TypeBox/JSON Schema generation path?
rationale: The choice defines an external API surface, versioning promise, and auth/scope exposure model, so automation should not pick the contract shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design Public Schema Contract First
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers choose schema format, exposure path, versioning model, and security boundary before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Static Artifact
options.body: Publish a committed or release-attached schema artifact for client generation without adding a runtime endpoint yet.

options.title: Defer To Existing Protocol Docs
options.body: Close later only if maintainers decide the TypeBox/JSON Schema pipeline and Gateway protocol docs are the intended client-generation surface.

recommendation.title: Design Public Schema Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers choose schema format, exposure path, versioning model, and security boundary before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` is the strongest current-main history signal for the Gateway protocol schema and HTTP routing surfaces that would define this contract.
